title: Bacterial extracellular vesicles from Streptococcus mutans drive OSCC progression through beta-catenin signaling.
authors: Cao, Guoding; Jiang, Yichen; Li, Xinhang; Liu, Ran; Liu, Kaili; Balcha, Fikadu; Ding, Mingyang; Yuan, Meng; Li, Ting; Fang, Yong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究变形链球菌胞外囊泡通过β-catenin信号促进口腔鳞癌进展，属于微生物-肿瘤信号通路研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is an aggressive malignancy in which microbial dysbiosis is increasingly recognized as a contributing factor, yet the pathogenic potential of bacterial extracellular vesicles (EVs) remains poorly defined. To determine whether Streptococcus mutans-derived EVs (SmEVs) influence OSCC progression, we isolated and characterized SmEVs from ATCC 35,668 and examined their effects in CAL-27 cells and a nude-mouse xenograft model. SmEVs were readily internalized by OSCC cells, enhancing their proliferative, migratory, and invasive capacities in vitro. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that SmEV exposure reshaped the CAL-27 gene expression landscape, prominently enriching the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway, accompanied by increased activation of beta-catenin, TCF7, and FOSL1/Fra-1 in both cultured cells and xenograft tumors. Functional loss-of-experiments further demonstrated that beta-catenin is critically required for these effects, as its silencing abrogated SmEV-induced proliferation, migration, and activation of the TCF7/Fra-1 axis. DIA proteomics identified a broad array of SmEV proteins, and in silico docking highlighted several abundant, cancer-associated candidates with strong predicted interactions with beta-catenin. In vivo, co-administration of SmEVs accelerated tumor growth and reinforced activation of the beta-catenin axis. Collectively, these findings provide the first evidence that S. mutans-derived EVs promote OSCC progression through beta-catenin-driven transcriptional programs and identify specific vesicular proteins as candidate mediators, offering new insights into microbe-derived factors as potential diagnostic or therapeutic targets in OSCC.
abstract_zh: 口腔鳞状细胞癌（OSCC）是一种侵袭性恶性肿瘤，微生物失调日益被认为是其促发因素之一，然而细菌细胞外囊泡（EVs）的致病潜力仍不明确。为确定变形链球菌来源的细胞外囊泡（SmEVs）是否影响OSCC进展，我们从ATCC 35,668中分离并表征了SmEVs，并在CAL-27细胞和裸鼠异种移植模型中检测了其效应。SmEVs可被OSCC细胞有效内化，在体外增强其增殖、迁移和侵袭能力。转录组分析显示，SmEV暴露重塑了CAL-27的基因表达谱，显著富集了Wnt/β-catenin信号通路，并在培养细胞和异种移植肿瘤中伴随β-catenin、TCF7和FOSL1/Fra-1的激活增强。功能缺失实验进一步证明，β-catenin对这些效应至关重要，因其沉默可消除SmEV诱导的增殖、迁移以及TCF7/Fra-1轴的激活。DIA蛋白质组学鉴定出广泛的SmEV蛋白，且计算机对接突出显示了多个丰富的、与癌症相关的候选蛋白，它们与β-catenin具有强预测相互作用。在体内，SmEVs的联合给药加速了肿瘤生长，并增强了β-catenin轴的激活。总体而言，这些发现首次提供了证据，表明变形链球菌来源的EVs通过β-catenin驱动的转录程序促进OSCC进展，并鉴定出特定囊泡蛋白作为候选介导因子，为微生物来源因子作为OSCC潜在诊断或治疗靶点提供了新见解。
